paper_metadata.title: Low-Phase-Noise LC Quadrature VCO Using Coupled Tank Resonators in a Ring Structure
paper_metadata.abstract: The concept of coupled resonators is employed in a ring VCO structure to reduce the phase noise. This architecture allows the design of low-phase-noise voltage controlled oscillators (VCOs) using integrated lowinductors. Quadrature differential outputs are also realized in this design. Two monolithic LC tanks are coupled together to implement a transimpedance resonator with an effective close to twice that of a single tank. In addition, the coupled tank’s transimpedance resonator provides 90 phase shift. Four such stages are cascaded in a ring structure to provide I–Q differential outputs, and to further reduce the phase noise. A prototype of the VCO is built in a 0.35m CMOS Fig. 1. Second-order transimpedance filter with series capacitive coupling. technology. The measured phase noise is 122 dBc/Hz at 600-kHz offset from 1.93 GHz. The VCO draws 9.2 mA from a 3-V supply, and occupies a chip area of 1.1 1.1 mm2. VCO architecture and its effect on phase noise are examined in Section III. In Section IV we discuss the implementation issues
